Agent consulted the blank-window guidance and removed <Window.SystemBackdrop><MicaBackdrop/> from MainWindow.xaml (session-log lines 3141, 4981).

tools_problematic.problem: Reported PASS on an app that renders a completely blank white client area. Section 7 only proves the process stayed alive; Section 9 only flags <Window.SystemBackdrop>, so it green-lit a window whose blank render came from a DIFFERENT composition-dependent scaffold feature (ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar + the new TitleBar control).
tools_problematic.evidence: score notes: parity_gate_verdict 'PASS (structural only, 100/100) — overridden by visual judgment: app renders blank'; validator .validator-diagnostics.txt empty, build PASS.

tool_limitations.limitation: Only detects <Window.SystemBackdrop>/MicaBackdrop/DesktopAcrylicBackdrop as the cause of the 'laid-out-but-blank-white in headless capture' symptom. It does not flag the sibling scaffold-added composition-dependent chrome — ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true + the dotnet-new-winui <TitleBar> control — which produces the identical symptom and survives backdrop removal.
tool_limitations.suggested_tweak: Extend Section 9 to also WARN when code-behind sets ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true and/or a scaffold <TitleBar> control is present but the UWP original used the standard title bar.

doc_errors.where: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md#system-backdrop-blank / SKILL.md 'Blank window even though the visual tree is fully populated'
doc_errors.wrong: Presents <Window.SystemBackdrop> as THE cause of the blank-in-headless-capture symptom and states removing it 'restores reliable rendering'. This over-promises: the agent removed the backdrop yet the window still renders blank white.
doc_errors.correct: Backdrop removal is necessary but not sufficient. The same symptom is also produced by other scaffold-added composition-dependent chrome (ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true + the new TitleBar control + SetTitleBar), none of which exist in the UWP source. For a UWP app that used the standard system title bar, revert the scaffold to a plain window as well.

special_apis.special_handling: Scaffolded by dotnet new winui but NOT present in typical UWP SDK samples (which use the standard title bar). Composition-dependent; keep only if the UWP original deliberately customized/extended the title bar. Otherwise remove for reliable headless-capture rendering and UWP parity.

errors_encountered.error: Migrated WinUI 3 app builds, launches, keeps its process alive, and lays out every control (UIA tree has all 6 + 4 controls with real bounding rectangles, x=774), yet the entire client area paints uniform white (10408-byte all-white frame); only OS caption buttons render.
errors_encountered.root_cause: A composition-dependent scaffold feature that survived the agent's Mica removal — ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true together with the dotnet-new-winui <TitleBar> control (added by the scaffold, absent from the UWP source) — fails to present the window content in the headless/VM/automated-capture session where parity screenshots are taken.
errors_encountered.fix: Generalize the blank-window fix: in addition to deleting <Window.SystemBackdrop>, remove the scaffold's title-bar customization (ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar=true, SetTitleBar, the <TitleBar> control) when the UWP original used the standard system title bar, so the window falls back to reliably-composited default chrome.

dev_agent_struggles.symptom: Agent identified blank-render risk, removed the Mica backdrop, saw validator PASS, and declared done — but the app still rendered blank.
dev_agent_struggles.turns_or_retries: single pass; agent believed the documented backdrop removal fully resolved blank render (session-log lines 3141, 4895, 4981)
dev_agent_struggles.root_cause: The skill told the agent that removing <Window.SystemBackdrop> 'restores reliable rendering', so it stopped after that one fix and did not consider the other scaffold-added composition-dependent chrome it left in place (ExtendsContentIntoTitleBar + TitleBar control).
dev_agent_struggles.preventable_by: Broadening the skill's blank-window section + validator Section 9 to cover all scaffold-added composition-dependent window chrome (backdrop AND extend-into-titlebar/TitleBar control), and softening the 'one fix restores rendering' language.

env_issues.issue: Parity screenshots are captured in a headless/VM/automated session where composition-dependent window chrome (Mica, and — per this trial — extend-into-titlebar/TitleBar) fails to present, blanking the whole window even though layout and process are healthy.
env_issues.workaround: Keep the migrated window on plain, reliably-composited default chrome unless the UWP original explicitly used the composited feature.
